panels.title: Sleep last night
panels.description: Minutes asleep in the night that ended this morning (yesterday's until today's arrives).

panels.title: Bedtime
panels.description: Time after the previous midnight, so 24 hours 30 min is 00:30.

panels.title: Sleep vs flow hours
panels.description: Does a short night cost flow? Sleep is the night ending that morning. Flow is molly:flow_minutes:increase1d, a trailing 24 hours.

panels.title: Sleep vs app switching
panels.description: Tired days tend to switch more. Switch rate is the 24 hour average of molly:switch_rate:5m, on the right axis.

panels.title: Bedtime
panels.description: Hours after midnight, so 24.5 is 00:30. No counterpart series yet: Molly has no recording rule for late-night work or gaming, so bedtime is shown alone.

panels.title: Stand hours vs unbroken active hours
panels.description: Molly cannot see steps by the minute, so the longest sedentary stretch is approximated by molly:active_unbroken_hours:1d: hours in the last day with no 5 minute idle gap.

panels.title: Steps vs active hours
panels.description: Long machine days and walking compete. Active hours on the right axis.

panels.title: Exercise vs commits
panels.description: Commits are the trailing 24 hours, so a day lines up only at its end.

panels.title: Daylight
panels.description: Minutes in daylight. No afternoon-focus series exists yet (no hour-of-day recording rule), so daylight is shown alone.

panels.title: Resting HR vs meeting hours
panels.description: A rising resting heart rate with a heavy meeting week is worth noticing. Seven day averages; meeting hours on the right axis.

panels.title: HRV vs interruptions
panels.description: HRV tends to fall when days are fragmented. Interruptions are the approximation in molly:interruptions:increase1h; seven day averages, on the right axis.
